title: Use same cache for Shader Editor and Script Editor
body:

## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Built on #121699 so its more clear how the logic is moved from the gui class to the singleton
- Follow up to #115998
- Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/122142

Shader editor now uses the same cache as the Script Editor `script_editor_cache.cfg` instead of `shader_editor_cache.cfg`.
Its cache was added in #115998 (cc @TheDying0fLight).
Using the same cache is cleaner IMO since they were basically the same and only being separated based on which editor a file was open in and not the actual file type.
This also makes it easier in the future to do things that need the same cache like opening shaders in the Script Editor or text files in the Shader Editor, or multiple editors. related https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2472

Also I happened to find and fix a few issues with debugger breakpoints:
Fixes renaming or removing a file right after adding its first breakpoint (without saving it to cache) did not update the breakpoint in the debugger. 
Fixes renaming after removing the last breakpoint (so the breakpoint is still saved in cache) adds a breakpoint to the debugger. 

Fixes renaming a script to a text file did not remove breakpoints, despite code checking for it. (There is still an issue where it opens with the wrong type of editor).

Fixes `restore_scripts_on_load` EditorSetting when false prevents deleted files from being removed from the cache and prevents breakpoints from unopened scripts from being loaded on startup in the debugger.

Fixes shader previews sometimes being set as breakpoints in the debugger on editor load. This one is a regression from #115998
To reproduce, the shader must be saved with a shader preview set, be part of an open scene, and be closed in the shader editor. And then reload the editor.


## Additional information

Using `ResourceLoader::exists(path, "Script")` is not a reliable way to determine if a file is a script, which caused a few of the above issues. Others were caused by using the cache when it is out of date.

`shader_editor_cache.cfg` was only added 4.8 so I didn't delete it (hoping this also gets into 4.8).

There is an existing issue where scripts with breakpoints that are opened but not the first document or the last selected document when reloading the editor don't set their breakpoints in the debugger. This is because they are not fully loaded, it should be fixed by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115662
